subject: Recap + next steps: pricing assumptions and who signs on budget
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: sofia.rinaldi@oddbox.ai, procurement@oddbox.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: pricing assumptions and who signs on budget

Hi Sofia — great chat today. Quick recap and the items we agreed to confirm: 

1) Estimated monthly token volume: 40–60M tokens (mostly text generation; ~5% embeddings).
2) Target unit price target: you mentioned a budget reference of $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on latency & quantization.
3) Key decision makers: you said product (Lina) owns the POC decision, while Finance signs commercial contracts — need name/role for finance approver.

What we need from you for a clean path to quote and contract: 
- Confirm the economic buyer (who approves spend for the model/POC).
- Confirm finance contact for billing/legal (name + email).
- Any compliance docs we must include aside from the NDA (you attached one; thanks).

Our ask from Redwood:
- We’ll send a quick SKU-level estimate for 40/60M token tiers with optional burst capacity and quantization tradeoffs (we’ll show $/1M token at each profile).
- We’ll include an ops playbook showing latency vs cost for the POC config you described.

Attachments: token runbook v2 (high-level sample rates) — see attached.

Proposed next steps: if you can confirm the finance approver by end of Tuesday (PST), we’ll share a formal quote and procurement checklist by Wednesday.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0211

-----Original Attachment: oddbox_token_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf) -----
From: Sofia Rinaldi <sofia.rinaldi@oddbox.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oddbox.ai, lina.martinez@oddbox.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:44:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: pricing assumptions and who signs on budget

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. A couple quick answers: 

- Economic buyer is Lina Martinez (VP Product). Lina leads the POC and will sign off on the business case.
- Finance approver is Marco Santos, Senior Finance Manager (marco.santos@oddbox.ai). He handles all contract approvals for 3rd-party platforms.
- Budget: current POC budget is $25k–$45k for the quarter; if we scale after POC, we’ll need to move to a program budget (TBD).

About pricing: the $700–$1,200/1M token range is generally acceptable as a starting point for the POC. Our main sensitivity is latency — if the POC needs sub-200ms median generation we understand price goes up.

Can you include a conservative and aggressive pricing column in the SKU table (i.e., quality/latency buckets) and highlight which SKU maps to the POC config Lina described? That will help Marco.

I’ve copied Lina and Marco here. Marco — can you confirm you’re the right finance contact and what procurement evidence you’ll need (PO, SOW, SOC2)?

Best,
Sofia
Head of Partnerships, Oddbox AI
sofia.rinaldi@oddbox.ai

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next steps: pricing assumptions and who signs on budget

Quick internal note — forwarding Sofia’s reply. Action items for us: 

- Jonas: build a 2-row SKU table for POC (conservative/aggressive) with $/1M token at 40M and 60M volumes; call out latency tradeoffs explicitly.
- Marissa: prep a short procurement checklist for Marco (PO template, SOC 2 link, sample SOW).
- Kimber: I’ll draft the cover email to Marco that frames the POC as low-risk and lists payment options (monthly vs prepay).

Also, confirm whether we should offer a small onboarding credit to keep initial spend within their budget band (25–45k). If yes, recommend a $5k credit tied to delivery milestones.

I’ll coordinate the email to Marco once Jonas attaches the SKU table and Marissa attaches the procurement docs.

— Kim
Kimberly Park | Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: pricing assumptions and who signs on budget

Hi Jonas / team — Marco here. Confirming I’m the right contact for finance approvals. For a POC at the scale you’re proposing we’ll need: 

1) A short SOW or statement of work (1–2 pages) that lists expected usage, acceptance criteria, and billing terms.
2) SOC 2 Type II evidence — our security team will need the report or a vendor portal link.
3) PO is preferred for this spend band; if Redwood requires invoices first we can discuss net-30 once procurement signs off.

On pricing: please send the SKU table with conservative/aggressive columns. Marco prefers unit math expressed as $/1M tokens and the overall expected monthly cost at both 40M and 60M so Finance can map to the budget.

If you want a fast path, include an optional onboarding credit line (we prefer credits applied to first invoice). If you include that, call it out clearly with milestone triggers.

Thanks — I’ll look for the docs and can expedite procurement review once the SOW and SOC2 link are in hand.

— Marco Santos
Senior Finance Manager, Oddbox AI
marco.santos@oddbox.ai
